title: Three capabilities, one dangerous combination
originalTitle: The lethal trifecta for AI agents: private data, untrusted content, and external communication
deck: An agent’s tool permissions can connect an attacker’s instructions to your private information.
takeaways: Private information, attacker-controlled input and an outbound channel create a data-theft path together.
Instructions embedded in retrieved material can redirect an agent.
Review combined tool permissions, not just individual tools.

sections.heading: How the path forms
paragraphs: A malicious document can ask an assistant to retrieve confidential information and transmit it. The tools supply the capabilities; injected instructions connect them.

sections.heading: Outbound channels hide in ordinary features
paragraphs: Email is only one route. Network requests, image loads and public repository activity can also carry information outward.

sections.heading: Inspect the combination
paragraphs: Willison warns that mixing tools can recreate vulnerabilities vendors previously closed. He questions detection promises because probabilistic protection leaves failures possible.
